exodus.4.p1.b1.text: What if they do not believe me or listen to my voice? For they may say, ‘The LORD has not appeared to you.’

exodus.4.p1.b2.text: What is that in your hand?

exodus.4.p1.b3.text: So Moses threw it on the ground, and it became a snake, and he ran from it.

exodus.4.p1.b4.text: Stretch out your hand and grab it by the tail, … and it turned back into a staff in his hand.

exodus.4.p1.b5.text: This is so that they may believe that the LORD, the God of their fathers … has appeared to you.

exodus.4.p2.b1.text: Put your hand inside your cloak.

exodus.4.p2.b2.text: when he took it out, his hand was leprous, white as snow.

exodus.4.p2.b3.text: when he took it out, it was restored, like the rest of his skin.

exodus.4.p2.b4.text: But if they do not believe even these two signs … take some water from the Nile and pour it on the dry ground. Then the water you take from the Nile will become blood on the ground.

exodus.4.p3.b1.text: Please, Lord, … I have never been eloquent, … for I am slow of speech and tongue.

exodus.4.p3.b2.text: Who gave man his mouth? … Now go! I will help you as you speak, and I will teach you what to say.

exodus.4.p3.b4.text: Is not Aaron the Levite your brother? I know that he can speak well, and he is now on his way to meet you. …

exodus.4.p3.b5.text: He will speak to the people for you. He will be your spokesman, … But take this staff in your hand so you can perform signs with it.

exodus.4.p4.b1.text: Please let me return to my brothers in Egypt to see if they are still alive.

exodus.4.p4.b3.text: Go back to Egypt, for all the men who sought to kill you are dead.

exodus.4.p4.b4.text: So Moses took his wife and sons, put them on a donkey, and headed back to Egypt. And he took the staff of God in his hand.

exodus.4.p5.b1.text: When you go back to Egypt, see that you perform before Pharaoh all the wonders that I have put within your power.

exodus.4.p5.b2.text: But I will harden his heart so that he will not let the people go.

exodus.4.p5.b3.text: this is what the LORD says: … Israel is My firstborn son

exodus.4.p5.b4.text: let My son go so that he may worship Me. But since you have refused to let him go, behold, I will kill your firstborn son!

exodus.4.p6.b1.text: Now at a lodging place along the way, the LORD met Moses and was about to kill him.

exodus.4.p6.b2.text: But Zipporah took a flint knife, cut off her son’s foreskin, and touched it to Moses’ feet.

exodus.4.p6.b3.text: Surely you are a bridegroom of blood to me

exodus.4.p6.b4.text: So the LORD let him alone.

exodus.4.p7.b1.text: Go and meet Moses in the wilderness.

exodus.4.p7.b2.text: So he went and met Moses at the mountain of God and kissed him.

exodus.4.p7.b3.text: and Aaron relayed everything the LORD had said to Moses. And Moses performed the signs before the people,

exodus.4.p7.b4.text: and they believed. And when they heard that the LORD had attended to the Israelites and had seen their affliction, they bowed down and worshiped.
